## Setup

------------------------------------------------------------------------

This homework is a Quarto document. You may work in RStudio on your computer or in Posit Cloud. Make sure `tidyverse` and `sf` are installed in your R environment. If you need to install either package, use the **Console**, not an `install.packages()` command in this document.

All data come from our course GitHub repository. The setup chunk below automatically downloads and extracts the Colorado county shapefile into `data/co_counties` when necessary. The companion shapefile files are handled for you. **You do not need to download, unzip, or upload data files manually.** In Question 2 you will import the CSV directly from GitHub using `read_csv()` and the URL stored in `data_url`.

Run the setup chunk before working on questions and whenever you start a new R session or render the document. An internet connection is required to import the CSV and to download the shapefile the first time.

```{r}
# Load packages used throughout the homework.
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(plotly)

# CSV location on the course GitHub repository. Import this in Question 2.
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CU-Denver-MathStats-OER/Data-Wrangling-and-Visualization/main/Data/cdc_co_healthcare_access.csv"

# Download the county shapefile and its companion files when needed.
county_zip_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CU-Denver-MathStats-OER/Data-Wrangling-and-Visualization/main/Data/co_counties.zip"
county_dir <- file.path("data", "co_counties")
county_parts <- paste0("Colorado_County_Boundaries.",
                       c("shp", "shx", "dbf", "prj", "cpg"))
county_files <- file.path(county_dir, county_parts)

if (!all(file.exists(county_files))) {
  dir.create(county_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  zip_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  download.file(county_zip_url, zip_file, mode = "wb")
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = county_dir)
  unlink(zip_file)
}

if (!all(file.exists(county_files))) {
  stop("County shapefile files are missing. Check the GitHub ZIP link.")
}
```

## About the Data: Healthcare Access and Preventive Services

------------------------------------------------------------------------

This assignment uses county-level data from [**CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release**](https://www.cdc.gov/places/index.html). The prepared CSV covers Colorado's 64 counties. PLACES reports **modeled prevalence estimates** derived from health surveys and population information. These are not direct counts of all residents and are not necessarily measurements collected during 2025.

All indicators in this assignment are **crude prevalence percentages**, not age-adjusted estimates. A value of `17.2` means **17.2%**, and does not need to be multiplied by 100. Importantly, **not all percentages refer to the same population**: some apply to all adults, while others apply only to adults in particular age or health-status groups.

### Data Dictionary

------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Variable | Description |
|----|----|
| `CountyName` | Colorado county name. |
| `CountyFIPS` | Five-character county identifier; preserve the leading zero in codes beginning with `08`. |
| `ACCESS2_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of adults **ages 18–64** with no current health insurance. |
| `DENTAL_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of **all adults** who visited a dentist or dental clinic within the previous year. |
| `CHECKUP_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of **all adults** who visited a doctor for a routine checkup within the previous year. |
| `CHOLSCREEN_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of **all adults** who had their cholesterol checked within the previous five years. |
| `BPMED_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of **adults with diagnosed high blood pressure** who report taking medication for high blood pressure. |
| `COLON_SCREEN_CrudePrev` | Estimated percent of **adults ages 45–75** who are up to date on colorectal cancer screening. |

The Colorado county shapefile includes `LABEL` (county name), `US_FIPS` (five-character county identifier), and county geometries.

::: callout-important
Higher percentages of reported care do not necessarily demonstrate better access or care quality. Geographic patterns in these modeled estimates also cannot demonstrate individual causes and effects.
:::

**Sources:** [CDC PLACES methodology](https://www.cdc.gov/places/methodology/) and [CDC prevention measure definitions](https://www.cdc.gov/places/measure-definitions/prevention.html). The 2025 release includes estimates based on earlier years of survey and population information.

::: callout-note
### Working with spatial data

Use `sf` for geometries and `dplyr` and `ggplot2` for data manipulation and visualization. If you use a pipe, you must use the native R pipe `|>` rather than `%>%`. Look at the plots and check your code output; a command that runs successfully can still produce a misleading map.
:::
